## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies, not actual organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages are separate processes with independent timelines.
- New worlds copy genome genes into a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving its genome and cellular-part archives, transfer features, and educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution tracks, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve the archive, cellular-part transfer, and educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS` descriptions and `runLab()` outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Reworded sample setup, prerequisites, and outputs for DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, gel, sequencing, gene expression, and viability; sample setup identifies assay-input proxies rather than collected biological samples.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`.

### Active
- Review remaining interface language in `index.html` and `app.js` for real-sample or measurement implications and consistent game framing.
- Retest genome archive and cellular-part transfer behavior, then verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Replace or clarify remaining language such as “FIELD STATION,” “SPECIMEN,” “VIABLE,” “observed cells,” “LIVE IMAGING,” “CULTURE DISH,” and “WET LAB.”
2. Review `doSequence()` prompts and notes, plus genome and cell view descriptions, for language implying real samples, measurements, or organisms.
3. Test archive and cellular-part transfers and verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, procedures, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.

## Important Context
- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- No tests or browser verification were reported after the latest copy changes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving its genome and cellular-part archives, transfer features, and educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve the archive, cellular-part transfer, and educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS` descriptions and `runLab()` outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Reworded sample setup, prerequisites, and outputs for DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, gel, sequencing, gene expression, and viability; sample setup identifies assay-input proxies rather than collected biological samples.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`.

### Active
- Review remaining interface language in `index.html` and `app.js` for real-sample or measurement implications and consistent game framing.
- Review `doSequence()` prompts and notes, plus genome and cell view descriptions, for language implying real samples, measurements, or organisms.
- Retest genome archive and cellular-part transfer behavior, then verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Replace or clarify remaining language such as “FIELD STATION,” “SPECIMEN,” “VIABLE,” “observed cells,” “LIVE IMAGING,” “CULTURE DISH,” and “WET LAB.”
2. Review sequence and genome/cell view copy for implications of real samples, measurements, or organisms.
3. Test archive and cellular-part transfers and verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, procedures, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- No tests or browser verification were reported after the latest copy changes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfer features, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfer, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS` descriptions and `runLab()` outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Reworded sample setup, prerequisites, and outputs for DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, gel, sequencing, gene expression, and viability; assay inputs are described as proxies, not collected biological samples.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Checked `index.html`, `README.md`, and `style.css` for terms implying real-world laboratory work, samples, or measurements; none found in `index.html`, while `README.md` explicitly states the limitations.

### Active
- Review remaining `app.js` wording, especially `doSequence()` prompts and genome/cell view descriptions, for implications of real samples, measurements, or organisms.
- Retest genome archive and cellular-part transfer behavior, then verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review remaining sequence and genome/cell-view copy, including `doSequence()`’s “Collect a sample and extract DNA” prompt.
2. Replace or clarify any remaining terms such as “SPECIMEN,” “VIABLE,” “observed cells,” “LIVE IMAGING,” “CULTURE DISH,” and “WET LAB.”
3. Test archive and cellular-part transfers and verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- No tests or browser verification were reported after the latest copy changes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfer features, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfer, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS` descriptions and `runLab()` outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Reworded sample setup, prerequisites, and outputs for DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, gel, sequencing, gene expression, and viability; assay inputs are described as proxies, not collected biological samples.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Checked `index.html`, `README.md`, and `style.css` for terms implying real-world laboratory work, samples, or measurements; none found in `index.html`, while `README.md` explicitly states the limitations.

### Active
- Review remaining `app.js` wording, especially `doSequence()` prompts and genome/cell view descriptions, for implications of real samples, measurements, or organisms.
- Retest genome archive and cellular-part transfer behavior, then verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review remaining sequence and genome/cell-view copy, including `doSequence()`’s “Collect a sample and extract DNA” prompt.
2. Replace or clarify any remaining terms such as “SPECIMEN,” “VIABLE,” “observed cells,” “LIVE IMAGING,” “CULTURE DISH,” and “WET LAB.”
3. Test archive and cellular-part transfers and verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- No tests or browser verification were reported after the latest copy changes.
- `cellView()` at `app.js` line 114 includes biological structure names, an `mmol/L ATP proxy`, ROS, and transcript targets; confirm the proxy framing is clear.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfer features, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfer, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS` descriptions and `runLab()` outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Reworded sample setup, prerequisites, and outputs for DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, gel, sequencing, gene expression, and viability; assay inputs are described as proxies, not collected biological samples.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Checked `index.html`, `README.md`, and `style.css` for terms implying real-world laboratory work, samples, or measurements; none found in `index.html`, while `README.md` explicitly states the limitations.
- Reviewed `cellView()`; it displays proxy values and genome-derived transcript targets, but remaining wording needs review for clarity.

### Active
- Review remaining `app.js` wording, especially `doSequence()` prompts and genome/cell-view descriptions, for implications of real samples, measurements, or organisms.
- Retest genome archive and cellular-part transfer behavior, then verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review remaining sequence and genome/cell-view copy, including `doSequence()`’s “Collect a sample and extract DNA” prompt.
2. Replace or clarify any remaining terms such as “SPECIMEN,” “VIABLE,” “observed cells,” “LIVE IMAGING,” “CULTURE DISH,” and “WET LAB.”
3. Test archive and cellular-part transfers and verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- No tests or browser verification were reported after the latest copy changes.
- `cellView()` uses biological structure names, an `mmol/L ATP proxy`, ROS, and transcript targets; confirm the proxy framing is clear.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfer features, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfer, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS` descriptions and `runLab()` outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Reworded assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs for DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, gel, sequencing, gene expression, and viability; assay inputs are described as proxies.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Checked `index.html`, `README.md`, and `style.css` for wording implying real-world laboratory work, samples, or measurements; `README.md` explicitly states the limitations.

### Active
- Review remaining `app.js` wording, especially `doSequence()` prompts and genome/cell-view descriptions, for implications of real samples, measurements, or organisms.
- Retest genome archive and cellular-part transfers, then verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review remaining sequence and genome/cell-view copy, including `doSequence()`’s “Collect a sample and extract DNA” prompt.
2. Replace or clarify terms such as “SPECIMEN,” “VIABLE,” “observed cells,” “LIVE IMAGING,” “CULTURE DISH,” and “WET LAB.”
3. Test archive and cellular-part transfers and verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- `cellView()` displays proxy values and genome-derived transcript targets; it uses biological structure names and an `mmol/L ATP proxy`, so confirm the proxy framing is clear.
- No tests or browser verification were reported after the latest copy changes.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfer features, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfer, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS` descriptions and `runLab()` outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Reworded assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs for DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, gel, sequencing, gene expression, and viability; assay inputs are described as proxies.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Checked `index.html`, `README.md`, and `style.css` for wording implying real-world laboratory work, samples, or measurements; `README.md` explicitly states the limitations.

### Active
- Review remaining `app.js` wording, especially `doSequence()` prompts and genome/cell-view descriptions, for implications of real samples, measurements, or organisms.
- Retest genome archive and cellular-part transfers, then verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review and revise remaining terminology, including “SPECIMEN,” “VIABLE,” “observed cells,” “LIVE IMAGING,” “CULTURE DISH,” “WET LAB,” and `doSequence()`’s “Collect a sample and extract DNA” prompt.
2. Test archive and cellular-part transfers.
3. Verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- `cellView()` displays proxy values and genome-derived transcript targets; it uses biological structure names and an `mmol/L ATP proxy`, so confirm the proxy framing is clear.
- No tests or browser verification were reported after the latest copy changes.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfer features, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfer, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS` descriptions, `runLab()` outputs, assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Revised overview copy to describe the microbial world as a game with independent model tracks.

### Active
- Review and revise remaining terminology that may imply real samples, measurements, or organisms, including `doSequence()` prompts and genome/cell-view descriptions.
- Test archive and cellular-part transfers, then verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Replace or clarify remaining lab-like wording such as “SPECIMEN,” “VIABLE,” “observed cells,” “LIVE IMAGING,” “CULTURE DISH,” “WET LAB,” and `doSequence()`’s “Collect a sample and extract DNA” prompt.
2. Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
3. Verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfer features, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfer, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS` descriptions, `runLab()` outputs, assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Revised overview copy to describe the microbial world as a game with independent model tracks.
- Updated the app description to “A procedural microbial-world game with independent, evolving model tracks.”

### Active
- Review remaining lab-like wording, including `doSequence()` prompts and genome/cell-view descriptions.
- Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
- Verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Replace or clarify remaining wording that could imply real samples, measurements, or organisms, such as “SPECIMEN,” “VIABLE,” “observed cells,” “LIVE IMAGING,” “CULTURE DISH,” “WET LAB,” and `doSequence()`’s “Collect a sample and extract DNA” prompt.
2. Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
3. Verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfers, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfers, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.
- Retain real-biology terminology and “sample” references within educational DNA Codex content.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS` descriptions, `runLab()` outputs, assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Revised overview copy to describe the microbial world as a game with independent model tracks.
- Updated the app description to “A procedural microbial-world game with independent, evolving model tracks.”
- Replaced multiple lab-like interface terms in `app.js` and `index.html`, including “SPECIMEN,” “VIABLE,” “LIVE IMAGING,” “CULTURE DISH,” and “LIVE CULTURE”; clarified sequencing inputs and cell-view readouts as simulated proxies.
- Reviewed current wording in `app.js`, `README.md`, and `index.html`; educational Codex references to real samples remain intentionally.

### Active
- Review remaining interface wording that could imply real samples, measurements, or organisms, especially `doSequence()` prompts and genome/cell views.
- Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
- Verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining interface language in `doSequence()` and genome/cell views, preserving educational Codex content.
2. Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
3. Verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- `cellView()` includes genome-derived transcript targets and proxy values, including “mmol/L ATP proxy”; some biological structure names remain.
- DNA Codex entries discuss real biology and use scientific terms such as “sample”; retain their educational content while reviewing game-interface wording.
- `rg` is unavailable; a search attempt returned `/bin/bash: rg: command not found`.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfers, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfers, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.
- Retain real-biology terminology and “sample” references within educational DNA Codex content.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS`, `runLab()` outputs, assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Revised overview copy to describe the microbial world as a game with independent model tracks.
- Updated the app description to “A procedural microbial-world game with independent, evolving model tracks.”
- Replaced multiple lab-like interface terms in `app.js` and `index.html`, including “SPECIMEN,” “VIABLE,” “LIVE IMAGING,” “CULTURE DISH,” and “LIVE CULTURE”; clarified sequencing inputs and cell-view readouts as simulated proxies.
- Reviewed current wording in `app.js`, `README.md`, and `index.html`; educational Codex references to real samples remain intentionally.

### Active
- Review remaining interface language that could imply real samples, measurements, or organisms, especially `doSequence()` prompts and genome/cell views.
- Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
- Verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining interface language in `doSequence()` and genome/cell views, preserving educational Codex content.
2. Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
3. Verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- `cellView()` includes genome-derived transcript targets and proxy values, including “mmol/L ATP proxy”; some biological structure names remain.
- DNA Codex entries discuss real biology and use scientific terms such as “sample”; retain their educational content while reviewing game-interface wording.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfers, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfers, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.
- Retain real-biology terminology and “sample” references within educational DNA Codex content.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS`, `runLab()` outputs, assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Revised overview copy to describe the microbial world as a game with independent model tracks.
- Updated the app description to “A procedural microbial-world game with independent, evolving model tracks.”
- Replaced multiple lab-like interface terms in `app.js` and `index.html`, including “SPECIMEN,” “VIABLE,” “LIVE IMAGING,” “CULTURE DISH,” and “LIVE CULTURE”; clarified sequencing inputs and cell-view readouts as simulated proxies.
- Reviewed wording in `app.js`, `README.md`, and `index.html`; educational Codex references to real samples remain intentionally.

### Active
- Review remaining interface language that could imply real samples, measurements, or organisms, especially `doSequence()` prompts and genome/cell views.
- Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
- Verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining interface language in `doSequence()` and genome/cell views, preserving educational Codex content.
2. Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
3. Verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- `cellView()` includes genome-derived transcript targets and proxy values, including “mmol/L ATP proxy”; some biological structure names remain.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfers, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfers, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfers, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfers, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.
- Retain real-biology terminology and “sample” references within educational DNA Codex content.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS`, `runLab()` outputs, assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Revised overview copy, app description, lab-like interface terms, sequencing inputs, and cell-view readouts to clarify simulated proxies.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` succeeds.

### Active
- Review remaining interface language in `doSequence()` and genome/cell views, preserving educational Codex content.
- Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
- Verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining interface language in `doSequence()` and genome/cell views.
2. Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
3. Verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- `cellView()` includes genome-derived transcript targets and proxy values, including “mmol/L ATP proxy”; some biological structure names remain.
- `doSequence()` assembles the simulated reference from `S.genome.sequence` after simulated DNA assay inputs are prepared.
- `/usr/bin/chromium` is available; Playwright is not installed.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfers, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfers, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.
- Retain real-biology terminology and “sample” references within educational DNA Codex content.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS`, `runLab()` outputs, assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Changed the overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Revised overview copy, app description, lab-like interface terms, sequencing inputs, and cell-view readouts to clarify simulated proxies.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` succeeds.

### Active
- Review remaining interface language in `doSequence()` and genome/cell views, preserving educational Codex content.
- Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
- Verify the redesign in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining interface language in `doSequence()` and genome/cell views.
2. Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
3. Verify the redesign in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- `cellView()` includes genome-derived transcript targets and proxy values, including “mmol/L ATP proxy”; some biological structure names remain.
- `doSequence()` assembles the simulated reference from `S.genome.sequence` after simulated DNA assay inputs are prepared.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfers, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfers, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.
- Preserve real-biology terminology and “sample” references within educational DNA Codex content.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS`, `runLab()` outputs, assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Changed overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Revised overview copy, app description, lab-like interface terms, sequencing inputs, and cell-view readouts to clarify simulated proxies.
- Inspected `doSequence()`, `cellView()`, `genomeView()`, archived-genome seeding, and cellular-part archive/install paths; no further changes made in this latest inspection.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` previously succeeded.

### Active
- Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
- Verify the redesign in a browser.
- Review whether remaining cell/genome interface wording needs adjustment, especially “A living sequence, transcribed and translated into phenotype” and cell readouts that may lack explicit proxy framing.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
2. Review remaining genome/cell copy for clarity that it describes game-generated proxies.
3. Verify the redesign in a browser and run applicable checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- Changes to `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` are uncommitted; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- `cellView()` already calls cell readouts and organelle entries proxies, but some values such as viability, membrane integrity, and ROS do not all carry explicit proxy labels in every display.
- `doSequence()` assembles the simulated reference from `S.genome.sequence` after simulated DNA assay inputs are prepared.
- `installCellPart()` blocks installing a proxy into its source cell and applies type-specific game-state effects; `archiveCellPart()` records proxy provenance.
- `newWorld(source)` creates a new state from the archived genome and does not restore the full archived world.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfers, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfers, and the educational Codex.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.
- Preserve real-biology terminology and “sample” references within educational DNA Codex content.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a GENESIS overview and limitations in `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent world and plate evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS`, `runLab()` outputs, assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs to describe simulated proxies.
- Changed overview control from “Collect sample” to “Prepare assay inputs” in `app.js`; updated navigation and global framing in `index.html`.
- Revised overview copy, app description, lab-like interface terms, sequencing inputs, and cell-view readouts to clarify simulated proxies.
- Inspected `doSequence()`, `cellView()`, `genomeView()`, archived-genome seeding, and cellular-part archive/install paths; no further changes made in the latest inspection.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` previously succeeded.

### Active
- Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
- Review remaining genome/cell copy for proxy clarity, especially “A living sequence, transcribed and translated into phenotype” and whether viability, membrane integrity, and ROS need explicit proxy labels in every display.
- Verify the redesign in a browser and run applicable checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
2. Review remaining genome/cell copy for proxy clarity.
3. Verify the redesign in a browser and run applicable checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- Changes to `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` are uncommitted; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- `cellView()` labels some readouts and organelle entries as proxies, but viability, membrane integrity, and ROS may lack explicit proxy labels in every display.
- `doSequence()` assembles the simulated reference from `S.genome.sequence` after simulated DNA assay inputs are prepared.
- `installCellPart()` blocks installing a proxy into its source cell and applies type-specific game-state effects; `archiveCellPart()` records proxy provenance.
- `newWorld(source)` creates a new state from the archived genome and does not restore the full archived world.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfers, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfers, and the educational Codex, including real-biology terminology and “sample” references within Codex content.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added GENESIS overview and limitations to `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS`, `runLab()` outputs, assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs as simulated proxies.
- Updated overview controls, navigation, app description, sequencing inputs, and cell readouts to clarify game-generated proxies.
- Added explicit proxy wording for membrane integrity, metabolic activity, ROS, protein-folding load, viability, damage, and cell readouts.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` succeeded.

### Active
- Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
- Verify the redesign in a browser and run applicable checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
2. Verify the redesign in a browser and run applicable checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- Changes to `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` are uncommitted; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- `doSequence()` assembles the simulated reference from `S.genome.sequence` after simulated DNA assay inputs are prepared.
- `installCellPart()` blocks installing a proxy into its source cell and applies type-specific game-state effects; `archiveCellPart()` records proxy provenance.
- `newWorld(source)` creates a new state from the archived genome and does not restore the full archived world.
- A local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; browser verification remains pending.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Rework GENESIS as a procedural microbial-world game while preserving genome and cellular-part archives, transfers, and the educational DNA Codex.
- Make clear that evolution, procedures, and readouts are independent simulated proxies—not real laboratory work or measurements.

## Requirements
- Frame GENESIS as a game, not an educational model or laboratory simulator.
- Preserve archives, cellular-part transfers, and the educational Codex, including real-biology terminology and “sample” references within Codex content.
- Explain that aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages have separate, independent timelines.
- Clarify that procedures and readouts concern simulated proxies, not an organism’s actual genome.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational game proxies, not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
- Aggregate population/genome evolution and plate-cell lineages follow separate processes.
- New worlds seeded from archived genomes create a fresh environment and plate; they do not resume a complete world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added GENESIS overview and limitations to `README.md`; updated game framing and proxy terminology across interface areas.
- Updated `evolutionView()` to distinguish independent evolution tracks and clarify fresh-world behavior for archived genomes.
- Revised `PROTOCOLS`, `runLab()` outputs, assay setup, prerequisites, and outputs as simulated proxies.
- Updated overview controls, navigation, app description, sequencing inputs, and cell readouts to clarify game-generated proxies.
- Added explicit proxy wording for membrane integrity, metabolic activity, ROS, protein-folding load, viability, damage, and cell readouts.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` succeeded.
- Started local server at `http://localhost:3002` and opened the app in Playwright; navigation to Cell viewer worked.

### Active
- Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
- Verify the redesign in a browser and run applicable checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test genome archive seeding and cellular-part archive/install transfers.
2. Finish browser verification and investigate any issues; the only observed console error was a missing `/favicon.ico` (404).

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Simulation logic, archives/transfers, and interface copy.
- `index.html`: Navigation and global game framing.
- `README.md`: Project overview and model limitations.
- `style.css`: Interface styling and cellular-part workbench.

## Important Context
- Changes to `README.md`, `app.js`, `style.css`, and `index.html` are uncommitted; preserve existing work.
- `tick()` evolves `S.genome`/`S.population`; `advancePlateCells()` separately evolves plate cells, whose genomes mutate on division.
- `doSequence()` assembles the simulated reference from `S.genome.sequence` after simulated DNA assay inputs are prepared.
- `installCellPart()` blocks installing a proxy into its source cell and applies type-specific game-state effects; `archiveCellPart()` records proxy provenance.
- `newWorld(source)` creates a new state from the archived genome and does not restore the full archived world.
- Playwright showed page title `GENESIS — Living Genome`; the sole console error was `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found) @ http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico:0`.
